subject: SIG: Business continuity / DR details for Medicorp (RTO/RPO, backups, failover)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@medicorp.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medicorp Security Team <security@medicorp.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: Business continuity questions — RTO/RPO and failover evidence

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is working through the SIG questionnaire and has a focused set of follow-ups on business continuity and disaster recovery. Can you confirm the following and attach any evidence we can include in the SIG response?

1) RTO targets for customer-facing inference API and for control-plane operations (in minutes).
2) RPO for token streams / in-flight sessions and for stored customer artifacts (logs, evals).
3) Backup cadence and retention for config/meta data (where it's stored, encrypted).
4) Regional failover: do you support automated cross-region failover for customer traffic, and what's the tested failover time?
5) Do you have an internal DR runbook and proof of at least one annual failover test we can point to in the SIG?

We're under a compressed timeline — procurement would like the SIG section completed this week. If you can point to a document or attach a short artifact that answers the items above, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Security and Compliance Manager
Medicorp Health

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@medicorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Business continuity questions — RTO/RPO and failover evidence

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short appendix and our internal runbook excerpt that map directly to SIG BCDR controls. Summary answers below (high level) — see attached for supporting artifacts and one-page test summary.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- RTO (objective):
  • Customer-facing inference API: 15 minutes for failover to warm standby within same region; 30 minutes for automated cross-region recovery to a designated secondary region for active customers.
  • Control plane operations (service management APIs): 60 minutes RTO for critical management paths (e.g., key rotations, model pinning rollback).
- RPO (objective):
  • Token streams / in-flight session state: designed to be near-zero for short sessions via persistent KV caching with replication; for long-running sessions we persist periodic snapshots — RPO target 5 minutes for stateful sessions.
  • Stored artifacts (logs, evals, config): backup snapshot cadence is nightly; RPO documented as 24 hours for non-critical artifacts, 1 hour for critical metadata (customer configs) when configured in high-durability mode.
- Backups & retention:
  • Metadata and config snapshots are taken nightly (incremental) and retained 90 days by default; encryption at rest using customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments.
  • Full backups of model-serving state (checkpoints) for Dedicated customers are retained per contract — typical baseline 30 days.
- Regional failover:
  • We support automated health-driven traffic routing to warm secondaries (cross-region). Warm standby capacity is maintained for Dedicated accounts and for high-priority tenants on Hosted (by plan). Automated failover end-to-end: tested target 30 minutes to resume 99% of API endpoints in the secondary region.
- DR runbook & testing:
  • We maintain a DR runbook (internal) and execute an annual cross-region failover test; we also run quarterly partial failover drills for core services. The attached appendix includes dates of the last two full DR exercises (June 2026, Dec 2025) and a one-page test summary.

Attachments included: redwood_sig_bcdr_appendix.pdf (one-page Q&A + test dates), runbook_nightly-backups.txt (excerpts), redwood_failover_topology.vsdx (diagram).

If you need numeric proof points (e.g., average observed failover times from the last run), Marissa can pull the test artifacts. Rishi can confirm encryption/retention options for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <l.chen@procure.medicorp.com>

Subject: Re: SIG: Business continuity questions — RTO/RPO and failover evidence

Soojin — procurement needs a couple of clarifications before we finalize the SIG appendix: please confirm the following in writing so we can close the control:

1) For the inference API, your RTO says 15 minutes (same-region warm standby) and 30 minutes cross-region. Is the 30-minute cross-region value a contractual SLA for Dedicated customers or a best-effort operational target for Hosted?
2) For backups: are nightly incremental backups atomic for metadata so config restores won't cause partial failures? Do you offer point-in-time restore windows for customer configs, and if so what is the maximum lookback?
3) Share the link/ID to the runbook exercise report from June 2026. We need a time-stamped artifact.

Can Marissa or Rishi respond with the specifics? Procurement prefers explicit wording we can paste into the SIG responses.

Thanks,
Lisa
Senior Procurement Manager
Medicorp Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <l.chen@procure.medicorp.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <dpark@medicorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Business continuity questions — RTO/RPO and failover evidence

Hi Lisa / Daniel / Soojin — Marissa from SRE here. Adding clarifications below you can paste into the SIG response fields. I've included links to the time-stamped exercise report and the snapshot manifest we referenced.

1) Cross-region RTO: 30 minutes is an operationally tested recovery target. For Dedicated contracts we offer an SLA-backed RTO option (contractual) — the SLA language and target are agreed per-customer on Dedicated plans. For Hosted accounts the 30-minute cross-region recovery is an operational target and included as part of our resilience program; we do not expose a hosted SLA for cross-region RTO by default.

2) Backups & atomicity: Nightly incremental backups of metadata are checkpointed and manifest-based to ensure atomic restores. We maintain a snapshot manifest for each backup job and use manifest replay to restore consistent state. Point-in-time restore for customer configs: available in high-durability mode with a 30-day lookback by default; can be extended per contract for Dedicated/Private customers (up to 365 days).

3) Runbook exercise report: the June 2026 full cross-region failover exercise (runbook id RB-2026-06-FR) is uploaded to our secure drive. Public link (time-stamped report): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ExampleJun2026Report

Supporting performance notes: during the June 2026 test we observed median failover completion for API endpoints of ~22 minutes (95th percentile 34 minutes) for the set of endpoints exercised. The attached appendix includes the one-page test summary.

Attachments (referenced in this thread): redwood_sig_bcdr_appendix.pdf (includes test metrics), runbook_nightly-backups.txt (manifest example), redwood_failover_topology.vsdx

If you need the raw logs/artifacts signed-off by our security team for procurement, we can produce a time-stamped bundle via secure transfer — let us know preferred mechanism.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Resilience Engineering
Redwood Inference
